leaves.doc: R11. Berger, Invent. Math. 148 (2002), Theoreme 0.7 = Cor. 5.22 of the published version (author copy pp. 6, 52) = Thm 0.6 = Thm 5.19 of arXiv:math/0102179v3, K = Q_p, for one p-adic representation V = E^n (E/Q_p finite inside Qbar_p, rho_E : G_Qp -> GL_n(E) continuous), for every generator eps0 = (1, zeta_p, zeta_p^2, ...) of Z_p(1) in O_Cp-flat: dim_Qp (B_dR (x) V)^{G_Qp} = dim V => there is a finite K/Q_p such that B_st (x)_Qp V has a B_st-basis of G_K-invariant vectors (Fontaine's B_st-admissibility, B_st (x) V = B_st^d equivariantly), with Berger's B_st = B_max[log p~], B_max = B_max^+[1/t], t = log [eps0], B_max^+ = A_max[1/p], A_max = {sum a_n (omega/p)^n : a_n in A_inf -> 0} inside Mathlib's B_dR

III section 1.4-1.5, numbering UNVERIFIED); de Rham as dim_Qp D_dR = dim V (K = Q_p; B_dR^{G_Qp} = Q_p proved, bdr-inv). pb-pst: one t (bmaxOf_eq, bstOf_eq: B_max inverting every log[eps] = B_max^+[1/t]); the dimension form dim_{B_st^{G_K}} D_st = dim V is proved from the basis form (isAdmissible_of_T), so no B_st^{G_K} = K_0 is used
